tasks.task: Look up the most recent papers related to 'cs.CL', select one and show its abstract.
tasks.answer: Selected paper from the most recent cs.CL papers: 'Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31646). Abstract: Many recent open-weight language models use n-gram embedding tables to improve performance. These tables store learned representations of short token sequences, such as pairs or triples of consecutive tokens, which the model retrieves during processing. However, they can require substantial memory: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, for example, allocates 196 billion parameters to its Engram n-gram memory. We therefore investigate whether this memory cost can be reduced while preserving the performance improvement that the tables provide. We propose storing n-gram embeddings at low precision and systematically investigate different quantization methods and bit allocations across tables. Across nanochat-, Llama-, and GPT-2-family models trained from scratch, four-bit tables save approximately 75% of table memory while preserving more than 99% of the validation-loss improvement from adding the tables. Using fewer bits leads to a larger drop in performance, although we find that a short fine-tuning phase recovers a significant part of this loss. In addition, reinvesting the saved memory in larger tables can improve performance beyond that of the original full-precision tables while still using less memory. These table memory savings also extend to large existing models: on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, low-bit tables save 47-55% of table memory, with perplexity increases of less than 1.2% and largely preserved downstream task performance. These findings establish low-bit precision as a practical way to reduce the memory requirements of n-gram embeddings and use the saved capacity to improve model performance.

tasks.task: Locate the most recent research paper about 'Algebraic Topology' under Mathematics published on ArXiv. Provide the title of the paper, the name of the authors, and the abstract.
tasks.answer:
The most recent research paper in Algebraic Topology (math.AT) under Mathematics on arXiv is:

Title: The center is the formal internal automorphism group
Authors: Sonja Farr
Abstract: We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.

(arXiv:2610.31411, listed first under the most recent date section on https://arxiv.org/list/math.AT/recent; abstract page https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31411)

tasks.task: Find the latest paper on 'machine learning in the Statistics section of ArXiv and provide its abstract.
tasks.answer:
Latest paper on 'machine learning' in the Statistics section of ArXiv (ordered by Announcement date, newest first):

Title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
arXiv ID: 2610.31663
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31663

Abstract: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent \alpha>1 and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared L_2 approximation rate \mathcal{O}((\kappa_P\log(m/\delta)/m)^\alpha) for two-layer networks of width m and trainable proportion P, where \kappa_P=(P/\kappa_1^*+(1-P)/\kappa_0^*)^{-1}. The bound holds uniformly over the unit ball of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with probability at least 1-\delta. The constants \kappa_0^* and \kappa_1^* quantify the fixed and trainable groups' sampling mismatches relative to the target RKHS. For spherical biased-ReLU features in dimension d, we verify these assumptions with \alpha=(d+2)/(d-1) and \kappa_0^*=4\sqrt{2}\tau(d+1)/d for initialization scale \tau\ge1, and \kappa_1^*=1 under ridge leverage sampling. For d=5 and \tau=10, a trainable proportion of approximately 4.1\% captures 90\% of the reduction in the approximation bound from P=0 to P=1. A structured three-layer example illustrates how a few trainable first-layer neurons exploit fixed downstream blocks through nonlinear composition. Numerical experiments across diverse settings, including networks with up to 15 layers, exhibit similar phase transitions in training errors.

tasks.task: Search for the most recent paper related to non-commutative geometry submitted by an author with the first name John. Provide the title and the abstract.
tasks.answer:
Title: Fuzzy Geometries with an Internal Space

Authors: John W. Barrett, Joseph Burridge (arXiv:2604.19549, submitted 21 April 2026 — the most recent result of an arXiv advanced search for 'non-commutative geometry' with author 'John', sorted by Announcement date newest first).

Abstract: The product of a non-commutative matrix spectral triple with a simple two-dimensional internal space is considered. This is interpreted as a non-commutative spacetime that contains one charged Dirac fermion and its antiparticle. The inner fluctuations of a vacuum Dirac operator are calculated, using the standard technique of Connes' one-forms. This results in the non-commutative analogue of a gauge field, as expected, and also fluctuations of the spacetime geometry. In addition, the fluctuations include a derivative operator that depends on the particle charge. The integral over the fermions in the model is calculated, leading to some novel induced bosonic terms.
